boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Ivy Mountain record (November 8-9, 1861) in Operations in Eastern Kentucky [September-December 1861]. Sill's march by John's Creek, the Piketon skirmish and Williams's retreat toward Pound Gap are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field describes the Union side as detachments from twelve units and the Confederates as nine companies of infantry and two of mounted men (1,010); the live field reads zero. Nelson says the enemy lay in ambush 700 strong. Williams's November 9 report says he had only about 300 against not less than 1,500, most probably 2,000, and gives his command as nine infantry and five mounted companies, 1,100 in all; on November 13 he says his whole force was 1,010 including sick and extra-duty men, that 250 held the Ivy position, and that the columns were 1,600 and 1,800.
claims.rationale: The CWSAC 1,010 matches Williams's November 13 whole-force figure, not the men engaged; his two reports differ on the mounted companies and on the men at the pass. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Colonel John S. Williams, Brigadier General William Nelson and Colonel Joshua W. Sill; the live page gives Nelson as Major General. Nelson ordered the Kentuckians to charge, Harris led his men up the mountainside and Norton moved up the northern ridge anticipating an order; Sill reached Piketon the night before Nelson. Williams went forward in person but returned to camp at daylight, and the pass was held by Captain May's party.
claims.rationale: Command roles from the two reports; the live rank is not adopted and there is no automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory (indecisive, but the Confederates withdrew); the live result reads Indecisive. Nelson says the rebels fled after an hour and twenty minutes and he pursued; Williams says his force was outflanked and fell back and the enemy did not pursue. Nelson places the fight at 1 p.m. on the 8th; Williams's November 9 report says 'yesterday' and his November 13 report says 1.30 on the 9th.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text and the live field read 293 (US 30; CS 263). Nelson reports his loss as a figure read '0' in OCR killed and 24 wounded, though he also says the first discharge killed 4 and wounded 13 of Marshall's men; he heard 32 enemy dead were found and took 6 unhurt prisoners. Williams first reports 10 killed and 7 or 8 wounded against at least 150 enemy killed, then 10 killed, 15 wounded and 40 missing against over 300 enemy killed.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Nelson's OCR-garbled killed figure is retained as printed in the scan.

open_questions: Sill's No. 2 report, Marshall's and the regimental reports, returns and maps remain deferred. No nineteenth-century history covering the action was selected; this is a two-report or two-family first pass.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Nelson's November 10, 1861 report is an interested Union account, the same author family as the registered Nelson Shiloh selections (group or-nelson). Williams's November 9 and 13, 1861 reports are one family of interested Confederate accounts, the same author family as the registered Williams Blue Springs selection. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
